air.title: Xeneta: Shippers want short-term deals as demand squeezes capacity
air.summary_en: Global airfreight volumes were up again in September and continued to outpace the increase in capacity, but shippers appear reluctant to commit to longer-term capacity deals, according to Xeneta. The analyst said that global airfreight volumes delivered another month of steady growth in September, up 6% year-on-year, continuing the upward trend seen in August and…
air.content: Global airfreight volumes were up again in September and continued to outpace the increase in capacity, but shippers appear reluctant to commit to longer-term capacity deals, according to Xeneta. The analyst said that global airfreight volumes delivered another month of steady growth in September, up 6% year-on-year, continuing the upward trend seen in August and July, when volumes rose 6% and 5%. Volume growth in September continued to outpace the increase in capacity, which rose 2% versus a year ago after flatlining in July and August. This contributed to a two percentage points increase in Xeneta’s dynamic load factor to 62%. Sustained demand has slowed anticipated rate reductions. Global air cargo spot rates averaged out as 27% higher than the same month last year. Rates edged up 2% month-on-month, consistent with the usual seasonal firming at the end of the third quarter and as jet fuel prices climbed due to continuing tensions in the Middle East to roughly double their pre-conflict level. Source: © Xeneta Alongside airfreight volumes outpacing capacity, Xeneta found most shippers were seeking short-term capacity contracts. Analysis of new contracts valid starting from the third quarter of this year shows 60% were for three months or less, compared with 25% in the third quarter of 2025 and 47% in the second quarter of this year. Three-month agreements alone accounted for 42% of new contracts, up from 16% a year earlier, while the share of 12-month contracts fell from 40% to 25%. Contracts of more than 12 months have all but disappeared, at 3%. Xeneta’s chief airfreight officer, Niall van de Wouw, said shippers are increasingly looking for ‘floating mechanisms’ with a base rate that’s adjusted depending on what’s happening in the marketplace. “There is a high degree of realism in the way shippers are approaching the market,” he said. “There remains a lot of instability and that’s making it almost impossible for shippers to make long-term capacity deals without having T&Cs in place to deal with these volatile conditions. “A one-year fixed rate deal doesn’t fit the current conditions. Shippers are looking to build mechanisms which add flexibility to their commercial relationships with forwarders, and which will help to ensure they hold across the year. “A one-year deal without any adjustment mechanism is becoming more the exception than the rule. If they do exist, not many will survive the upcoming 12 months.” Source: © Xeneta E-commerce insights Xeneta’

air.title: Central Asia air cargo demand growth presents charter challenges
air.summary_en: Air cargo demand in the central Asia region has been on the rise in recent years, but building charter operations to meet the growing number of infrastructure projects does have its challenges. Speaking at the Central Asia Air Cargo Summit, Chapman Freeborn vice president of cargo for the India, Middle East, Africa region Gerhard Coetzee…
air.content: Air cargo demand in the central Asia region has been on the rise in recent years, but building charter operations to meet the growing number of infrastructure projects does have its challenges. Speaking at the Central Asia Air Cargo Summit, Chapman Freeborn vice president of cargo for the India, Middle East, Africa region Gerhard Coetzee highlighted the speed of demand growth in the region. He said that the region needs to invest around $33bn annually in infrastructure projects while trade through the so-called Middle Corridor is set to triple by 2030. Growth in mining, energy, infrastructure and manufacturing is also creating more demand for heavy, oversized, time-critical and project cargo, he added. “The important point is that cargo demand is increasingly being generated inside Central Asia – rather than simply passing through it,” said Coetzee. “Every one of these sectors creates a different type of cargo requirement, and not all of that cargo can move efficiently through a scheduled network.” Coetzee added that while connectivity to and from central Asia is improving, with China increasingly connected with Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, and scheduled links with Europe are also developing, that does not always mean the right type of capacity is available. He said this is particularly important for project cargo as an aircraft may have sufficient available payload, but the cargo may be too large for the aircraft type, the required route may not be available at the right time, or the airports involved may not have the infrastructure to handle the movement. “There is an air cargo network, but it isn’t necessarily designed around the cargo that these new industries are generating,” Coetzee said. He explained that a scheduled service may work well for standard freight, but a heavy industrial component moving to a remote destination against a project deadline creates a different requirement altogether. There are also airport limitations when it comes to handling larger aircraft such as the Boeing 747s, Boeing 777s and AN-134s. Cargo such as a 70-tonne transformer or 16-metre pipes requires suitable loading equipment, runway capability and specialist handling. Permits and regulatory approvals add another layer, while winter weather and de-icing can affect both timing and operating cost, he said. Coetzee concluded that as Central Asia becomes more integrated into global supply chains, the challenge will not simply be how much air cargo capacity exists

air.title: GSSAs set for closer airline integration
air.summary_en: GSSAs will evolve to increasingly integrate with airlines while offering a menu of services and target new market entrants, according to speakers at the Aviation Connect event. During a panel discussion at the Athens event, speakers were asked how they felt GSSAs would develop in the future. Kales Group chief executive Sebastiaan Scholte said that…
air.content: GSSAs will evolve to increasingly integrate with airlines while offering a menu of services and target new market entrants, according to speakers at the Aviation Connect event. During a panel discussion at the Athens event, speakers were asked how they felt GSSAs would develop in the future. Kales Group chief executive Sebastiaan Scholte said that new entrants to the airline industry could become future customers of GSSAs. He explained that over recent years shippers, shipping companies, e-commerce platforms, freight forwarders and ACMI providers have all emerged as aircraft operators. “All of them have certain lanes that are not full and they also have directional imbalances, so what I see as a future role for GSSAs is to become a broker of capacity. Who better can commercialise this space?” he said. Elsewhere, Scholte said GSSAs would increase their use of AI tools to help improve aircraft utilisation while they would also increasingly sell back-office services to airlines. The industry will also increasingly act as a “virtual airline”, he said. “Many airlines want a Total Cargo Management (TCM) solution where you are the de facto cargo department of the airline. The advantage of a GSSA is that, if you do it right, you will take the best of all the airlines you represent and you become the best so-called virtual airline.” His view was echoed by Vitaly Smilianets of Awery Aviation Software, whose product is utilised by many GSSAs. “I think that GSSAs will offer more and more TCM solutions, and I think it is happening more and more in the last two to three years,” Smilianets said. “The next succession for the GSSAs is that they can take over and do everything for the airline. “Airlines will get to a point where they not only outsource their sales capabilities for a specific country but outsource the whole story and even do it globally.” Smilianets also felt that airlines would increasingly use GSSAs for financial services, such as payment collection. Emma Oliver, managing director of TCM provider Northwind Global Logistics, said that GSSAs of the future would have an important role to play in creating a single source of data across the industry. “I think that where GSSAs can use the technology to become a better extension of the airline is where they will be able to differentiate themselves. “Whether that is using the platform of an airline or using their own technology to ensure seamless messaging so we have this one source of truth, one source of data, a

rail.title: Kazakhstan anticipates an increase in transit traffic following the launch of the modernized Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway.
rail.content: gov.kz Kazakhstan participated in the official opening of the modernized Baku–Tbilisi–Kars (BTK) railway line, which serves as one of the key elements of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR). At the ceremony, held on June 2 at the Akhalkalaki station in Georgia, the country was represented by Zhanbiek Taizhanov, Vice-Minister of Transport of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The upgraded line is designed to expand transport capabilities connecting Central Asia, the Caucasus, Turkey, and Europe. gov.kz The Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway establishes a direct link between the railway networks of Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey, thereby creating additional opportunities for delivering Kazakhstani cargo across the Caspian Sea to European markets. For Kazakhstan, the development of this route holds strategic importance, as it contributes to strengthening the country’s transit potential, increasing the volume of international freight traffic, and enhancing the efficiency of logistics chains across the Eurasian region. The total length of the railway line is 827 km. Following its launch in test mode in 2017, the line underwent extensive modernization, which was carried out from May 2023 to May 2024. As a result of this reconstruction, the route’s throughput capacity has increased fivefold – from 1 million to 5 million tons of cargo per year – opening up new opportunities for growth in cargo flow along the Middle Corridor and for the further development of international transit through Kazakhstan. Source: https://www.gov.kz/?lang=ru

rail.title: KTZ has more than doubled its profits and continues the large-scale modernization of its network.
rail.content: АО «Самрук-Қазына» Talgat Aldybergenov, Chairman of the Management Board of JSC NC Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, presented the company’s performance results at a meeting of the Public Council of JSC Samruk-Kazyna. For the year 2025, the national railway operator demonstrated growth across all key operational and financial indicators. Freight turnover increased by 7%, traffic volume rose by 6%, transit shipments grew by 20%, and export shipments by 7%. The company’s revenue for the year increased by 27%, while net profit grew 2.1-fold. This positive trend continued into the first quarter of 2026. One of KTZ’s key priorities remains the renewal of its rolling stock. Between 2023 and 2025, the company acquired 433 locomotives, a move that enabled it to reduce the wear rate of its locomotive fleet from 66% to 58%, boost productivity, and improve network operational performance. The modernization of the passenger sector is also ongoing: over the past two years, the wear rate of passenger carriages has dropped from 46% to 36%, and plans are in place to further expand the fleet with another 746 new carriages by 2030. Concurrently, KTZ is implementing a major railway infrastructure development program. Currently, construction is underway on approximately 900 km of new railway lines, alongside the modernization of around 3,000 km of existing tracks, which includes the installation of automatic block signaling systems. Key projects include the Darbaza–Maktaaral, Moyinty–Kyzylzhar, and Bakhty–Ayagoz lines, as well as the Almaty station bypass railway line. Several modernized sections – including Kyzylzhar–Sekseul, Altynkol–Zhetigen, and Aksu–Zhana-Semey – have already been commissioned ahead of schedule. Source: https://rail-news.kz/ru

rail.title: KTZ is expanding its railway infrastructure amidst growing traffic between China and Europe.
rail.content: ЦТС Kazakhstan’s national railway operator, KTZ, is accelerating the implementation of infrastructure projects to boost transit traffic between China and Europe. According to company head Talgat Aldybergenov, interest among Chinese shippers in land-based routes has grown significantly due to their greater reliability and predictable delivery times compared to maritime transport. Another factor driving the redistribution of cargo flows has been instability along traditional transport corridors, which has reinforced Kazakhstan’s role as a key transit hub within the Eurasian region. One of the primary routes remains the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, the importance of which has increased substantially since 2022. In response to this growing demand, KTZ is implementing a large-scale modernization program for its railway network. By 2030, infrastructure investments are projected to reach $10 billion, with approximately half of this amount already utilized. This year alone, the company is constructing 900 kilometers of new railway lines, including the 300-kilometer Ayagoz–Bakhty section, which will establish a third railway crossing between Kazakhstan and China. Upon the completion of these projects, the throughput capacity along the Kazakhstan–China corridor is expected to rise from the current 55 million tons to 100 million tons of cargo per year. KTZ also plans to expand the capabilities of the Trans-Caspian Route. While approximately 173 container trains traveled along the corridor during the first quarter, the company expects to raise this figure to 600 trains by year-end, and to increase it by nearly another two-thirds the following year. To support these growing traffic volumes, the operator intends to acquire hundreds of locomotives, six cargo vessels for operations on the Caspian Sea, and a cargo aircraft, as well as to expand its logistics facilities at ports in China and Europe. Source: https://cfts.org.ua/

rail.title: KAZLOGISTICS participated in a discussion on the digital future of Kazakhstan’s transport and logistics system.
rail.content: KAZLOGISTICS Kanat Almagambetov, CEO of the Union of Transport Workers of Kazakhstan (KAZLOGISTICS), participated in a roundtable discussion dedicated to the integration of science, education, business, and industrial logistics. The event took place on May 22 in Almaty at the M. Tynyshpayev ALT University, bringing together representatives from government agencies, the scientific community, educational institutions, and the business sector to discuss prospects for the development of the country’s transport and logistics industry. During the plenary sessions and panel discussions, participants addressed issues regarding the digital transformation of the transport and logistics complex, the development of multimodal transport, the training of qualified personnel, the implementation of ESG approaches, and the expansion of collaboration between the scientific community and the business sector. Particular attention was paid to establishing a unified digital architecture for the industry and building a modern transport and logistics system for Kazakhstan – one grounded in digital technologies, effective cargo flow management, and the integration of industrial logistics. KAZLOGISTICS emphasized the importance of uniting the efforts of industry organizations, educational institutions, and the expert community to implement practical initiatives aimed at advancing the transport sector. Following the meeting, the parties discussed the prospects for joint projects and pilot solutions designed to further digitize and enhance the efficiency of Kazakhstan’s transport and logistics system. Source: https://kazlogistics.kz/ru

rail.title: Germany’s dependence on Chinese imports continues to grow, contrary to its diversification strategy.
rail.content: Daimler Trucks In recent years, Germany has deepened its reliance on supplies of strategically vital goods from China, despite the government’s stated objective to mitigate economic risks and diversify supply chains. This conclusion was reached by experts at the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom, an organization affiliated with Germany’s Free Democratic Party (FDP). The study was published ahead of a visit to China by Germany’s Minister of Economic Affairs, Katharina Reiche, and reveals that the share of Chinese imports across a range of critical goods continues to rise. According to the analysis, the share of lithium-ion battery supplies from China increased from 49.7% in 2023 to 66.5% in 2025. A similar trend is evident in the pharmaceutical sector: the share of Chinese antibiotics rose from 65.3% to 72.9%, while imports of vitamins and provitamins also saw significant growth. This dependency is particularly pronounced in the solar panel segment, where China already accounts for 92.6% of total imports by weight. Furthermore, China effectively remains Germany’s sole supplier of the rare earth elements praseodymium, neodymium, and samarium – materials essential for manufacturing high-performance permanent magnets used in electric motors and other high-tech products. Over a two-year period, the volume of imports for these materials more than quadrupled – rising from 3.1 tons in 2023 to 13 tons in 2025 – underscoring the deepening reliance of German industry on Chinese raw materials. Source: https://transportjournal.com/

rail.title: The modernization of transport infrastructure will boost the development of tourism in Kazakhstan.
rail.content: KAZLOGISTICS At a government meeting, measures to develop transport infrastructure in support of the tourism industry were reviewed. According to Minister of Transport Nurlan Sauranbayev, roadworks this year have covered 11,000 km of public roads, including access routes to the Rakhmanovskie Klyuchi, Kenderli, Bayanaul, Zerenda, and Kolsai tourist areas. The completion of the Almaty–Ust-Kamenogorsk highway has reduced travel time by 4–5 hours, thereby improving the region’s transport accessibility. Plans are in place to complete the modernization of railway stations in Kokshetau, Borovoye, Konayev, Balkhash, and several other cities by July 1. Additionally, the procurement of 191 new railcars and the launch of 15 summer routes will create over 400,000 extra passenger seats, helping to meet rising demand during the tourist season. In the aviation sector, construction of tourist-oriented airports is underway in Katon-Karagai, Zaysan, and Kenderli, alongside the restoration of the Arkalyk airport and the modernization of the terminal in Urdzhar. The Minister noted that domestic flights play a key role in regional connectivity; during the summer season, 45 subsidized flights operate weekly to destinations including Alakol, Balkhash, Turkistan, Burabay, and the Caspian Sea coast. Source: https://kazlogistics.kz/ru

rail.title: Baku-Tbilisi-Kars railway reopens after Georgia section capacity increases five times.
rail.content: ADY The Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway reopened on June 2 after modernization works on the Georgian section of the corridor. Azerbaijan Railways carried out the works in 2024 on the 184 km section of the BTK railway in Georgia. The project increased the corridor’s annual freight capacity from 1 million tonnes to 5 million tonnes. The five-phase modernization covered 13 railway stations, 55 bridges, eight traction substations and 320 buildings. It also included engineering structures such as overpasses and crossings. The works included 30.3 km of new track, the construction of a wheelset-changing facility, and the rehabilitation and reconstruction of 153.1 km of existing railway infrastructure. The BTK railway opened in 2017 as a rail link between Azerbaijan, Georgia and Türkiye. It forms part of the Middle Corridor route linking China and Central Asia with Europe. Source: https://railmarket.com/

rail.title: The Port of Barcelona and Shanghai have signed a strategic logistics partnership agreement.
rail.content: Port of Barcelona The Port of Barcelona Authority has entered into a new strategic cooperation agreement with the Shanghai Municipal Transportation Commission (SMTC) and the Shanghai International Port Group (SIPG). Signed during a visit by a Shanghai delegation, the document aims to strengthen the long-standing partnership between these two major port hubs in Europe and Asia. Representatives from port authorities and regional officials from Catalonia participated in the ceremony. The agreement formalizes their “sister port” status and expands cooperation in key areas, including the digitalization of port operations, enhanced security, the development of environmentally sustainable infrastructure, and the adoption of alternative fuels. Particular emphasis is placed on developing intermodal transport and establishing “green” and digital maritime corridors between the Far East and the Mediterranean, a move designed to boost the efficiency of global logistics chains. Cooperation between the parties has been actively developing since 2025, following the signing of a preliminary memorandum and subsequent technical visits to Barcelona by SIPG delegations. During the most recent visit, the Shanghai representatives toured port facilities, including the Auto Terminal and the Free Trade Zone. The signing of this new agreement solidifies Barcelona’s role as a key logistics hub in the Euro-Mediterranean region and strengthens its ties with Shanghai, one of the world’s largest ports. Source: https://transportjournal.com/

rail.title: The EEC discussed new stages of transport integration among EAEU countries.
rail.content: eec.eaeunion.org At the 31st meeting of the Consultative Committee on Transport and Infrastructure of the Eurasian Economic Commission (EEC), participants examined key areas for the further development of transport integration within the Eurasian Economic Union. The meeting was chaired by EEC Minister for Energy and Infrastructure Arzybek Kozhoshev and attended by deputy heads of relevant transport agencies from EAEU member states. Discussions focused on the digitalization of the transport sector – including the implementation of electronic document management systems – as well as the development of high-speed railway lines and expanded cooperation with international organizations. These areas are viewed as crucial elements for enhancing transport efficiency and strengthening the Union’s transit potential. Committee members were also briefed on the progress of drafting a new roadmap for implementing a coordinated transport policy among EAEU states for the 2027–2029 period. Furthermore, participants reviewed the implementation of the action plan associated with the Declaration on the Further Development of Economic Processes up to 2030 and the long-term “Eurasian Economic Path” strategy up to 2045, both of which aim to establish a unified transport space and develop international logistics routes. Source: https://rail-news.kz/ru

rail.title: China’s Jiangsu International Rail Freight Express is expanding cooperation with the Trans-Caspian route.
rail.content: TITR A meeting took place at the headquarters of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR) Association with a delegation from the Chinese company Jiangsu International Rail Freight Express Co., Ltd. During the meeting, the parties discussed developing cooperation and attracting additional cargo flows to the Trans-Caspian route. The Chinese delegation was led by the company’s General Manager, Xia Jin; representatives of the company’s logistics and supply chain management divisions also participated in the talks. Representatives from Jiangsu International Rail Freight Express presented the capabilities of Jiangsu Province’s international railway network, which operates under the “Four Directions – Eight Corridors” model. The network comprises 26 regular international routes spanning 26 countries, as well as approximately 80 logistics terminals located along the transport corridors of the Belt and Road Initiative. The company coordinates operations at key logistics hubs in Lianyungang, Xuzhou, Nantong, Suzhou, and Nanjing, facilitating multimodal transport via rail, road, sea, and air. Particular attention was paid to the potential of the Port of Lianyungang, a member of the TITR Association. The parties noted the opportunity to utilize its infrastructure to establish new logistics chains connecting Japan, South Korea, Central Asian countries, Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey, with subsequent cargo delivery to European markets. Following the negotiations, the participants reaffirmed their interest in strengthening the partnership and agreed to continue joint efforts to enhance transport efficiency and increase cargo volumes along the TITR route. Source: https://middlecorridor.com/en/

rail.title: HHLA’s METRANS expands intermodal terminal in Poznań/Gadki, Poland.
rail.content: HHLA HHLA subsidiary METRANS has completed a major expansion of its intermodal terminal in Gądki near Poznań, increasing both storage and handling capacity at the important hub. The project added two remote-controlled railway gantry cranes, extended the existing rail infrastructure and expanded storage and service areas. As a result, maximum storage capacity has grown from 8,850 TEU to 11,800 TEU, while annual handling capacity has risen by almost 80% to around 590,000 TEU. The upgraded terminal now has two 80-metre-span gantry cranes, a dedicated crane runway with power supply and remote-control station, as well as two additional tracks. The three existing tracks were extended to more than 750 metres, allowing the terminal to handle the longest freight trains. METRANS also added 53,000 m² of paved operational areas, camera-based gate systems for automated container identification and condition recording, a rail weighbridge for monitoring axle loads and a container weighing system. According to METRANS Group CEO Peter Kiss, the investment will strengthen connections between seaports and customers across Central Europe and support reliable intermodal freight transport. Gądki is a key hub in METRANS’ European intermodal network, linking the Polish market with major economic centres across Europe. Poland’s economy grew by 3.6% in real terms in 2025 and has a GDP of around €923 billion, making it the EU’s sixth-largest economy. The terminal expansion was co-financed under Poland’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (KPO). METRANS currently operates terminals in 15 European countries, with its network extending from the North and Baltic seas to the Adriatic and Black seas, and transported 1.6 million TEU in 2025. Source: https://hhla.de/en

rail.title: CLIP Group opens South Poland Terminal Zabrze in Poland.
rail.content: CLIP CLIP Group has officially opened South Poland Terminal Zabrze, a new intermodal facility developed on the former site of the Makoszowy coal mine in Zabrze, Poland. The opening ceremony was attended by Wojciech Staniszewski, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of CLIP Group; Agnieszka Hipś, President of the Management Board of CLIP Group; Kamil Żbikowski, Mayor of Zabrze; Jarosław Siergiej, President of the Management Board of the Szczecin and Świnoujście Seaports Authority; and Sławomir Piątek, President of Torkol. The investment marks another step in the development of Poland’s transport infrastructure and more resilient supply chains. The terminal features modern cargo handling yards, an extensive rail track system and supporting facilities designed to integrate rail and road transport. CLIP Group expects the facility to increase freight handling efficiency and capacity, support the growth of intermodal transport in Poland and strengthen the competitiveness of rail freight. The terminal will handle both domestic and international cargo flows while improving Poland’s connectivity with key European transport corridors. The project received nearly PLN 72.5 million in financial support from the European Union under the NextGenerationEU programme. The investment is intended to strengthen Poland’s logistics network, support regional and national economic development and enhance the resilience of transport infrastructure and European supply chains. Source: https://clip-group.com/en/home/

rail.title: Nurminen Logistics and Tarros Group launch intermodal corridor between Northern Europe and the Mediterranean.
rail.content: Nurminen Logistics Nurminen Logistics and Tarros Group have established a new intermodal transport corridor connecting the Nordic countries with the Mediterranean region. The new service is now available for booking and offers transportation in both directions using rail, road and sea. The companies have integrated Nurminen Logistics’ Sweden–Italy rail service with Tarros Group’s inland transport, terminal and maritime network. The new model allows customers to arrange the entire logistics chain through a single provider, eliminating the need to coordinate multiple carriers and operators separately. The door-to-door service covers rail, road and sea transport, terminal handling, freight forwarding and customs clearance. According to Marjut Linnajärvi, VP International Rail Operations and Sales at Nurminen Logistics, the companies coordinate every stage of the journey to simplify the management of complex international logistics chains for customers. The partnership is designed to create a more integrated and coordinated transport solution between northern and southern European markets. By combining Nurminen Logistics’ rail network with Tarros Group’s operations in Italy and the Mediterranean, the companies aim to provide customers with easier access to multiple transport modes and improve the efficiency of freight movements between the two regions. Source: https://transportjournal.com/

rail.title: EU plans to invest up to €12 billion in the development of the Middle Corridor.
rail.content: ЦТС European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced a new EU project to develop the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR), also known as the Middle Corridor, in her annual address to the European Parliament. Through the Global Gateway initiative, the EU plans to mobilise up to €12 billion in public and private investment to strengthen transport connectivity between Europe, the Caucasus and Central Asia. The project aims to diversify transport routes, triple trade flows and significantly reduce cargo transit times by 2030. According to von der Leyen, amid major global changes, Europe’s prosperity and security depend not only on developments within individual countries but also on stronger international connections and transport infrastructure. The European Commission also plans to organise a Regional Summit on Transport Connectivity to advance the initiative. The event is expected to provide a platform for further discussions on investments and joint projects aimed at developing the Middle Corridor and strengthening its role in trade links between Europe and Central Asia. Source: https://cfts.org.ua/

rail.title: TRACECA and Ukraine discuss transport infrastructure recovery and logistics resilience in the Black Sea region.
rail.content: TRACECA On 18 September 2026, Jasurbek Choriev, Secretary General of the Permanent Secretariat of the Intergovernmental Commission TRACECA, met with Yurii Husiev, Ambassador of Ukraine to Azerbaijan, at the Embassy of Ukraine in Baku. The meeting focused on regional transport priorities, stronger institutional cooperation and joint measures to improve the resilience of logistics chains in the Black Sea region along the Europe–Caucasus–Asia route. Particular attention was given to restoring the full operation of Ukraine’s port and railway infrastructure to facilitate the uninterrupted movement of cargo between Asia and Europe via the Caucasus, as well as in the opposite direction. Choriev highlighted the need to remove infrastructure barriers and coordinate efforts among the countries participating in the transport corridor. He also stressed the role of the Black Sea region as a link within the wider TRACECA network and the Middle Corridor. The meeting also covered digitalisation and standards harmonisation. The sides noted Ukraine’s active participation in implementing the TRACECA Basic Multilateral Agreement and additional arrangements to facilitate transit transport, as well as the need to harmonise approaches to developing digital ecosystems along the corridor using UN standards for the digitalisation of multimodal transport corridors. The participants also discussed the TRACECA initiative to establish regional Competence Centres in member states. The Ukrainian side supported the initiative, highlighting its importance for digital development and the training of specialised personnel. Following the meeting, Ukraine and TRACECA expressed their interest in continued coordination to strengthen transit stability, improve the regulatory framework and develop further transport cooperation. Husiev also invited the Secretary General of the TRACECA Permanent Secretariat to visit Ukraine. Source: https://traceca-org.org/en/home/

rail.title: Fuel oil shortage puts further pressure on the marine bunker market.
rail.content: TELS The global fuel oil market is facing tightening supply as refiners affected by wars and disruptions to crude processing and tanker traffic increasingly prioritise diesel and other higher-value products. Strikes and attacks affecting refineries in Russia and the Middle East, combined with restrictions on tanker movements, have pushed refined product prices higher. China is also reducing refining capacity and exports in an effort to preserve domestic stocks. The shift towards more profitable products is putting additional pressure on fuel oil availability. According to Reuters data, fuel oil inventories at major trading hubs including Singapore, Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp and Fujairah are already around 30% below their three-year seasonal averages. Falling stocks and rising prices reflect the growing imbalance between supply and demand for the marine fuel. Tighter fuel oil supplies could increase costs for shipowners and power generators already dealing with disruptions caused by conflicts. Higher bunker fuel prices could also raise operating expenses for shipping companies and put additional upward pressure on freight rates as carriers pass part of the increased fuel costs through to customers. Source: https://telsglobal.com/

rail.title: Accelleron completes more than 100 projects with new ACCX300-L turbocharger.
rail.content: Accelleron Accelleron has completed more than 100 projects with stakeholders across the shipping industry just four months after the commercial launch of its new ACCX300-L turbocharger. The projects involve shipowners, engine manufacturers and shipyards. Designed specifically for two-stroke marine engines, the turbocharger has already been integrated into the configurators of leading engine manufacturers and selected by shipyards and engine builders in China and South Korea. The commercial launch of the ACCX300-L took place in April 2026, with the first deliveries from the current order backlog scheduled for March 2027. The ACCX300-L offers higher power density and features a service-friendly cartridge system that allows the entire rotating assembly to be replaced during a vessel’s port stay, reducing the need for extensive maintenance work in dry dock. Accelleron has also reduced the number of frame sizes from five to two, providing greater flexibility and helping customers plan lifecycle costs more efficiently. According to Christoph Rofka, President of Accelleron’s Medium and Low Speed Division, the rapid adoption of the new turbocharger reflects the growing focus among customers on efficient operation and maintenance of equipment over its entire service life. The ACCX300-L comes as standard with Turbo Insights, enabling data-driven maintenance and integration with Accelleron’s service offerings, including Turbo MarineCare, from the time of delivery. The turbocharger is available in both single and dual configurations. In the dual setup, automatic switching on and off at low engine loads can improve efficiency and reduce specific fuel consumption during slow steaming operations. Source: https://transportjournal.com/

rail.title: KTZ presents Middle Corridor development plans at investment forum in Baku.
rail.content: KTZ Yerlan Koishybayev, Deputy Chairman of the Management Board of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ), took part in the Azerbaijan International Investment Forum in Baku, where he presented the results and development prospects of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR), also known as the Middle Corridor. During a panel discussion on regional connectivity, he highlighted the route’s role in strengthening transport and logistics links between Central Asia, the Caucasus and European markets. In the first eight months of 2026, around 44,000 TEUs were transported along the TITR, representing a 58% increase compared with the same period last year. According to Koishybayev, the TITR is developing into an integrated multimodal transport system connecting railway, port and maritime infrastructure across several countries. KTZ and its partners are working to improve the route’s efficiency by developing rail and terminal infrastructure, expanding and modernising rolling stock, increasing port capacity and improving the maritime component. Other measures include fixed tariffs, digitalisation of processes and closer coordination between the different elements of the route. One of the key initiatives is the establishment of Middle Corridor Multimodal Ltd., involving railway companies from Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Georgia and China. The company is developing a unified operational approach to transportation, including coordinated schedules and single responsibility towards customers. During the forum, KTZ representatives also discussed with international businesses and financial institutions further development of transport connectivity and measures to improve the efficiency of transit routes. Source: https://rail-news.kz/ru

rail.title: Kazakhstan starts Aktau port dredging to lift Middle Corridor cargo 30%
rail.content: 2026 October 6 Dredging has begun at Kazakhstan’s Port of Aktau on the Caspian Sea, with about 1.3m cubic metres of material to be removed and the harbour basin deepened to 6–7 metres, according to the country’s Ministry of Transport. The work is aimed at countering the continuing decline in the Caspian Sea level, which is affecting navigation and operating conditions at the port. The project is expected to support growth of up to 30% in cargo volumes on the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, or Middle Corridor, and create conditions for a 10%–15% reduction in the cost of the maritime leg. Completion is targeted by the end of 2026. The dredging is also intended to improve navigation safety and support further investment in port infrastructure. Chinese contractor China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd (CHEC) is carrying out the project. Preparatory work included geodetic surveys, data processing and mobilisation of specialised dredging vessels, machinery and equipment. At that stage, 680 metres of a planned 785-metre containment embankment at the reclamation site had been completed. Kazakhstan is targeting an increase in Middle Corridor capacity from 6m tonnes to 10m tonnes by 2028. Container traffic between China and Europe using the route increased by 30% in the first five months of 2026. CHEC is a subsidiary of China Communications Construction Company (CCCC), a Chinese state-owned engineering and construction group. JSC NC Aktau International Sea Commercial Port is a Kazakh state-owned port operator within the Kazakhstan Temir Zholy group. It has 11 berths and annual cargo-handling capacity of 11.8m tonnes, handling crude oil and petroleum products, metals, grain and rail-ferry cargo. Latest news 2026 October 5 2026 October 4

rail.title: Panama Canal opens long-term booking to Panamax locks for first time
rail.content: The Panama Canal will extend its Long-Term Slot Allocation programme to the Panamax locks for the first time, with a pilot covering transit dates from 3 January to 3 April 2027, according to an authority statement. The Panamax LoTSA programme will offer 51 packages covering 288 transit slots, comprising 147 northbound and 141 southbound passages. That equates to an average of three LoTSA slots per day. The packages will be awarded through a sealed-bid competition on 24 November 2026. Bidding will run from 10:00 to 14:30 Panama time in staggered 30-minute cycles, with the first priority booking window opening on 16 December. All Panamax packages will be offered at a single Fixed flexibility level, with an initial base price of $60,000 per slot. Eligible segments include dry bulk ships, tankers, LPG carriers, full containerships, vehicle carriers and ro-ro vessels, as well as other qualifying vessels. The pilot is limited to Super-category vessels using the Panamax locks, with a maximum overall length of 294.44 metres and beam of 32.61 metres. Panamax Plus vessels are not eligible. The highest bidder for each package will secure the allocation, while submission time will determine the winner where bids are identical. The existing Neopanamax LoTSA programme will offer 36 packages covering 270 slots, split between 165 northbound and 105 southbound transits. Its sealed-bid competition is scheduled for 17 November, with the first priority booking window opening on 29 November. The Panamax pilot will use the same allocation mechanism, selection criteria and tie-breaking rules as the Neopanamax programme. Unsold Panamax packages will be reconfigured for a second LoTSA round, with any remaining capacity returning to the regular reservation system. Advisory A-37-2026, signed by Panama Canal Authority vice president for operations Boris Moreno Vásquez, also changes the late-booking cancellation surcharge from 15 October. The threshold will be cut from seven days to four days or less before the required arrival time, while the surcharge will remain at 250% of the reservation fee. The Panama Canal Authority is an autonomous public-law entity of the Republic of Panama responsible for the administration, operation, conservation, maintenance and modernisation of the canal under Panama’s constitution and the ACP Organic Law of 1997.

rail.title: Jordan, UAE break ground on $2.5bn mining rail link to Aqaba port
rail.content: 2026 October 6 Construction has started on a $2.5bn, 403-km railway linking mining and logistics centres in southern Jordan with the Port of Aqaba, according to an Abu Dhabi government statement. The Jordan-UAE Railway Company is developing the Aqaba-Al-Shidiyeh-Maan project, which will connect the port with mining and production sites and the Maan Logistics Zone. The first phase is expected to carry about 13m tonnes of phosphate a year from Shidiya to Aqaba. The wider network is designed to move about 16m tonnes of phosphate and potash annually, providing a rail link between production centres and Aqaba for exports to regional and global markets. The project includes about 55 bridges and six tunnels. It is expected to create about 5,000 jobs in southern Jordan and cut annual phosphate and potash transport costs by around $40m. The latest project scope is larger than the plan agreed in April, when investment was put at $2.3bn for a 360-km network linking the Al-Shidiya phosphate mining area and Ghor Al-Safi potash production area with the Port of Aqaba. The first phase will also connect with the planned Maan Land Port. The Jordan-UAE Railway Company was established in April 2026 as the joint venture responsible for implementing, operating and maintaining the network. Etihad Rail is its executing arm for the project. Etihad Rail is the developer and operator of the UAE national rail network. It was established in 2009 under UAE Federal Law No. 2 with a mandate covering the development, construction and operation of the country’s freight and passenger railway network. rail.title: Greek car carrier Neptune Ethos grounds off Salamina in Greece with 36 aboard
rail.content: 2026 October 6 Greek-flagged car carrier Neptune Ethos grounded on a sandy seabed off Salamina in Greece on Monday evening with 36 people aboard, according to the Hellenic Coast Guard. The 36 comprised 27 crew members and nine members of a private repair team. All were safe and in good health. Neptune Ethos had sailed from Elefsina without cargo after undergoing maintenance and was heading towards open water when it grounded in the Kamatero area near the channel serving the Salamina naval base. The cause of the grounding has not been established. Three tugboats and a Coast Guard craft were sent to the scene, while a private diver was deployed to inspect the vessel ahead of refloating efforts. No confirmed damage to the ship had been disclosed. Neptune Lines said the grounding caused no marine pollution and posed no threat to the environment. The company was working with the relevant authorities and specialist contractors to manage the incident under applicable safety procedures. Piraeus-based Neptune Lines is a Greek vehicle logistics and shipping company founded by Nikos Travlos in 1975 and chaired by Melina Travlos. Its network covers more than 50 ports in 27 countries, while its fleet comprises 21 pure car and truck carriers. Neptune Ethos was built in China in 2011. Neptune Lines acquired the vessel, formerly named Hoegh Singapore, in 2022 and subsequently placed it under the Greek flag. Latest news 2026 October 5 2026 October 4

rail.title: Royal Caribbean and MSC start building joint cruise terminal in Japan
rail.content: Royal Caribbean Group and MSC Cruises have started construction of a new cruise terminal at Naha Port in Okinawa through their Cruise Port Naha G.K. joint venture, according to a company statement. The formal groundbreaking took place on 2 October 2026 at the port’s Second Cruise Berth. The terminal is scheduled for completion and the start of operations in March 2028. The facility is being built at Shinko Wharf No 12, where the berth is 430 metres long and has a water depth of 12 metres. Cruise Port Naha G.K. signed a Cruise Hub Formation Agreement with Naha Port Authority on 28 August 2026. The agreement runs until 31 March 2058. Naha Port was designated an International Cruise Ship Hub Formation Port by Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism in 2019. The project is intended to increase passenger-handling capacity and support cruises starting and ending in Okinawa, including fly-and-cruise operations. Okinawa Governor Genta Koja, who is also president of Naha Port Authority, attended the groundbreaking alongside representatives of Japan’s Cabinet Office, the port authority and the two cruise groups. Royal Caribbean Group chairman and chief executive Jason Liberty said Japan was “one of the most important cruise markets in Asia.” Pierfrancesco Vago, executive chairman of MSC Group’s Cruises Division, said the project formed part of the group’s long-term plan to expand its presence in Asia and create year-round cruise opportunities in the region. Royal Caribbean Group operates 71 ships serving more than 1,000 destinations through Royal Caribbean, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea, and holds a 50% interest in TUI Cruises. Geneva-headquartered MSC Cruises is privately owned and operates 23 ships serving more than 300 destinations in more than 100 countries. Cruise Port Naha G.K. is a joint venture between CTL Maritime and RCL Cruises Ltd.

rail.title: At least 22 dead after passenger boat sinks in DR Congo river collision
rail.content: 2026 October 6 At least 22 people have died after a commercial boat and a passenger riverboat collided on the Congo River in western Democratic Republic of Congo, sinking the passenger vessel, according to a report citing provincial interior minister Chrispin Mputu. The collision occurred near Ngombe in Lukolela territory, Equateur province, at about 2am local time on Saturday. The commercial vessel was operating between Kinshasa and Mbandaka, while the passenger boat was travelling from Mongala province to Kinshasa. The passenger vessel was carrying 163 people. Twenty-two bodies had been recovered and buried and 59 people rescued, while the wreck remained submerged at a depth of 12 metres. Recovery operations were continuing on Monday evening, and Mputu said other victims might have been buried elsewhere. An earlier official account identified the vessels as the metal boat Dieu se cache, which had come from Kinshasa, and the wooden HB Super Victoire, which had travelled from Businga in South-Ubangi province. It said HB Super Victoire capsized while carrying about 100 passengers and gave a provisional toll of about 10 dead, several missing and 57 survivors. The same account identified night navigation and the absence of signal lights as possible causes. Search teams were working to recover missing people and bodies from the submerged vessel. A separate account quoting Mputu put the death toll at at least 30 and said those killed had already been buried, with dozens still missing. The differing passenger and casualty figures mean a final toll has yet to be established. River transport is a main form of travel and trade across much of western DR Congo, where many communities lie along the Congo River. Overcrowding and poor vessel maintenance are recurring factors in river accidents. Latest news 2026 October 5 2026 October 4

rail.title: Lloyd’s Register backs GasEntec’s 1-bcfd FSRU concept with AiP
rail.content: GasEntec has secured approval in principle from Lloyd’s Register for an LNG floating storage and regasification unit designed to send out up to 1bn cubic feet of gas per day, according to an LR statement. The approval followed LR’s independent assessment of the design’s technical and safety fundamentals and was presented during Gastech 2026 in Bangkok. The concept combines high send-out capacity with a multi-mode regasification system capable of operating in open, closed and combined-loop modes. The configuration is intended to allow operators to adapt the unit to different environmental conditions, regulatory requirements and project needs. GasEntec has based the concept on a modular architecture that can be configured for different capacities, pressures and operating requirements. If delivered, the FSRU would be among the world’s largest by send-out capacity. “This FSRU delivers a common modular platform that can be configured for different capacities, pressures and operating conditions, enabling efficient project specific engineering and faster deployment,” GasEntec co-chief operating officer TG Kim said. “As energy demand accelerates around the world, from grid growth to AI data center driven power needs, the constraint isn't supply; it's how quickly and reliably you can get gas to where it's needed.” GasEntec plans to use its first LR AiP to advance the FSRU design towards execution and support projects for FSRU owners and developers. LR global gas technology director Jose Navarro said: “As developers look to bring LNG import capacity online quickly, operators need solutions that can perform reliably across different climates, weather conditions and regulatory environments. This design combines very high send-out capacity with operational flexibility, helping to address some of the key challenges facing future FSRU projects.” LR global offshore business director Sean Van der Post said: “As countries seek secure and flexible routes to LNG supply, concepts such as this reflect how FSRU development is evolving beyond capacity alone, with greater emphasis on flexibility, adaptability and long-term operational resilience. “By independently assessing new designs at an early stage, we help give developers, investors and operators confidence as they progress projects from concept towards deployment.” Lloyd’s Register provides independent technical and safety assessment services for maritime and offshore projects, including early-stage design approval. GasEntec develops engineering concepts for LNG infrastructure, including floating storage and regasification projects.

rail.content: 2026 October 5 Prior trials confirmed the vessel meets design specifications Photo credit: the USC press office United Shipbuilding Corporation says that its Nizhny Novgorod based Krasnoye Sormovo Shipyard delivered another RSD59 series vessel. These vessels are capable of operating on both inland waterways and in maritime areas. According to the Volgo-Don Max class, the RSD59 ships possess the maximum dimensions permitted for the Volga-Don Shipping Canal, ensuring optimal cargo capacity utilization while adhering to inland waterway restrictions. These vessels are designed to transport a broad range of cargo, including general and bulk cargo (grain), packaged lumber, round timber, scrap metal, metal in bundles and coils, oversized and heavy lift loads, coal, dangerous goods, and Category B cargo. Their versatile cargo capabilities ensure operational flexibility, allowing the vessels to operate effectively across various routes, including within multimodal logistics chains. Key particulars of RSD59 vessel: LOA: 140.88 m; Beam: 16.98 m; Depth: 6 m; FW/SW DWT: 5,128/7,535 tonnes; FW/SW draft: 3.6/4.53 m; Cargo hold capacity: 11,292 m³; Number of holds: 2; Endurance: 20/12 days. rail.title: Britain’s most recognised freight operation turns twenty
rail.content: Rail freight operator DRS, headquartered in Carlisle and part of Nuclear Transport Solutions, began servicing the giant retailer Tesco with a single service in 2006. Since then, the now famous “Tesco Trains” have grown into one of the UK’s most successful rail freight operations. The operations now cover up to ten services per day, running from the locations in the south of England to the north of Scotland. Over the last 20 years, the collaboration has helped remove hundreds of thousands of lorry journeys from Britain’s roads, reducing congestion and significantly lowering carbon emissions. Each intermodal train on the route removes around forty heavy goods vehicles from the road network. The trains have become among the most photographed freight operations in the UK, especially on the Highland Main Line , between Perth and Inverness. The latter destination is dominated by the supermarket chain, and is often referred to, impolitely, as “Tesco Town”. Direct Rail Services and Tesco have a long-term contract in place for delivery of goods by rail – although not triple stacked. Image: © DRS However, despite the daily arrival of a train of branded containers at the Inverness terminal, much of the load is destined for outlying retailers in the remote parts of northwest Scotland. The flow is often cited as a prime example of ‘final mile’ operations, backed by a trunk delivery by rail, with produce on board coming from as far away as Tesco’s main distribution hub at Daventry, in the so-called Logistics Golden Triangle in the English Midlands. Supermarket sweep The occasion was marked earlier this week with the unveiling of a new name for locomotive 88010, now called “Tesco 20 years of rail freight”, at Tesco’s Daventry terminal. NTS’s co-CEO Ciara Middlehurst and Tesco’s Mathew Rhind, UK Transport Distribution Director, revealed the new nameplate. “It is an absolute pleasure to celebrate this significant milestone. Direct Rail Services has been Tesco’s trusted rail partner from the very beginning,” said Ciara Middlehurst, Co-CEO of Nuclear Transport Solutions (NTS), owner and operator of DRS. “Together we have built one of the most recognisable and successful rail freight partnerships in the country.” The rail and retail operators recently renewed their long-term contract for goods delivery. Tesco containers loading at Daventry Intermodal Rail Freight Terminal (DIRFT). Image: © Network Rail According to DRS, innovation has been a key driver throughout the partnership. DRS has continually invested in new operating models, wagon designs and technologies to improve performance and sustainability. The company was also the first rail freight operator in the UK to introduce a mainline overhead-powered bi-mode locomotive with its Class 88 fleet . This is particularly significant for ‘fast-moving consumer goods’ as the route between Daventry and Inverness is only partially electrified. The Class 88 is capable of hauling up to 1,500 tonnes of freight with zero exhaust emissions when operating under electric power, comfortably more than even the most enthusiastic supermarket sweep.

rail.title: Bulgaria, Greece and Romania prioritise €22.8bn of corridor projects
rail.content: Bulgaria, Greece and Romania identified 25 transport projects to prioritise to strengthen links between the Aegean, Danube and Black Sea regions. The estimated combined value is €22.8 billion and rail projects account for the largest share of the 25 items. The projects form part of the Black Sea–Aegean Sea Corridor Platform established by the three countries a year ago. The initiative is intended to improve north-south connections between Greek ports, Bulgaria, Romania and onward routes towards Moldova and Ukraine. Three routes The programme envisages three principal routes: western, central and eastern. The western axis would connect Thessaloniki with Sofia and the Romanian network through Vidin/Calafat and Craiova. The central axis would link the Greek port and Alexandroupoli with Svilengrad, Ruse, Giurgiu and Bucharest, with onward connections towards Ukraine and Moldova. The eastern axis would connect Alexandroupoli with Svilengrad and Bulgaria’s Black Sea ports at Burgas and Varna, continuing towards Constanţa. The projects Among the priority railway projects is the modernisation of the Ruse–Giurgiu–Bucharest connection, including electrification of the existing Danube railway-road bridge, opened in 1954. The project is expected to seek CEF funding, with implementation currently envisaged for 2028–30. The programme also includes plans for a second Danube bridge between Ruse and Giurgiu, with completion targeted for 2032. Feasibility work is being supported through EU funding, including military-mobility programmes. Railway infrastructure in Greece. Image: © ERGOSE On the Bulgarian network, modernisation of the Burgas–Varna–Ruse railway is intended to increase capacity and speeds, with electrification, ERTMS and double-tracking. The programme also includes preparatory work for additional Danube crossings. Greek priorities include upgrading the Alexandroupoli–Pythio–Ormenio line towards the Bulgarian border, with a construction contract expected in the first quarter of 2027, and improvements on the Mouries–Promachonas–Kulata route towards Sofia. A rail connection between the Port of Thessaloniki and the national railway network is also being advanced. The priorities The three countries are targeting infrastructure capable of supporting longer and heavier freight trains, with the memorandum establishing the corridor platform referring specifically to 740m freight trains, ERTMS, interoperability, multimodal terminals and digital logistics systems. The €22.8bn figure represents the estimated value of the 25 priority projects rather than committed investment. The projects were selected from an initial portfolio of 53 proposals. Bulgaria, Greece and Romania intend to seek additional EU financing under the 2028–34 financial framework and CEF.

rail.title: Italy unveils its first DAC demo train
rail.content: Italian state-owned operator FS Logistix presented its first demo train in the context of Digital Automatic Coupling (DAC). “With Italy’s first DAC demo train, we are bringing a tangible example of European railway innovation to Bologna,” said the company’s CEO Sabrina De Filippis. The demonstration of DAC operations took place at Interporto Bologna, one of the 10 largest intermodal terminals in Europe. This is the first showcase of the train in preparation for the tests planned in Italy for next year. Six locomotives and 120 wagons will be equipped with the coupler for intermodal services. Will the skepticism end? The tests were first announced in June 2024 , sparking skeptical reactions from many in the industry, who argued that funds could be better deployed to help the current financial difficulties most operators continue to face. Rail freight volumes in Italy have been going down for a few years now, especially due to capacity restrictions tied to infrastructure works, leaving companies stranded. FS Logistix CEO Sabrina De Filippis. Image: © FS Logistix On the other hand, there have been significant DAC developments in the past two years. Commercial tests have been completed in Germany , while Rail Cargo Group tasked Knorr-Bremse with equipping 23 wagons and one locomotive to run real commercial operations from 2028. Poland, Luxembourg, Slovenia, Sweden and Norway are also committed to run or already running DAC pilots.

rail.title: APM Terminals launches new rail service in Denmark
rail.content: APM Terminals Aarhus and the Port of Aalborg agreed on launching a rail service between the two locations. “Initially, the train will arrive and depart once a week. During the coming period, the partners will also assess market demand and the potential for additional departures”, APM said. The APM site in Aarhus is Denmark’s largest container terminal, while the inland port of Aalborg is the largest of its kind in the country. The new service is part of the Inland Hub Northern Jutland initiative launched by the Maersk subsidiary and the port of Aalborg. The project aims to link the Northern Jutland area to Aarhus and contribute to the modal shift to rail, APM added. Moreover, the new connection will provide an additional alternative to shippers. “Going forward, they can use both the direct feeder service to Hamburg and the direct rail connection to Denmark’s largest container port in Aarhus and the international transport networks linked to it”.

rail.title: New TEN-T plans reveal how far Europe is slipping beyond 2030
rail.content: The European Commission has released its latest TEN-T corridor work plans, putting firmer dates on where Europe’s rail network is likely to miss the legally binding 2030 core-network deadline. RailFreight.com picks out ten of the most important updates. The European Commission has published its new generation of TEN-T corridor work plans , showing where each corridor stands and what still needs to be done. The picture is mixed: three corridors explicitly acknowledge that full compliance by 2030 will not be achieved, while several of Europe’s biggest rail projects are now scheduled beyond the 2030 deadline. ERTMS deployment also remains particularly far behind. Here are ten of the key updates from the new plans. 1. Three corridors explicitly concede that 2030 will be missed The Atlantic , Baltic Sea–Black Sea–Aegean (BBA) and Western Balkans–Eastern Mediterranean (WBEM) work plans all acknowledge that their current project pipelines will not deliver full TEN-T compliance by 2030. The Atlantic plan says “full compliance of the core network will not be reached” by the 2030 milestone. Key stretches are expected to be completed by 2034, but some projects extend to 2040 and beyond, while 20 still have no confirmed completion date. The outlook differs further east. The WBEM plan says there are “reasons to assume” all sections could meet the required parameters by 2040, although this will need to be reassessed in future work plans. The BBA assessment is more pessimistic: it says the projects currently identified will not be sufficient to achieve full compliance and operation by either 2030 or 2040. Image: © Wikimedia Commons 2. ERTMS remains far behind the 2030 target If the new corridor plans show the scale of the challenge project by project, ERTMS presents an even starker network-wide picture. The Commission’s separate ERTMS work plan was published in February, but its figures underline the same trajectory. ETCS was operational on only around 10% of the EU TEN-T network at the end of 2024. Even with another roughly 28,000 km planned before 2030, the ERTMS coordinator says current planning would achieve “only about 50%” of the core-network target. The Atlantic Corridor illustrates how that plays out at corridor level. Just 31% of the entire corridor is currently expected to have ETCS in operation by 2030, rising to only 39% by 2040. 3. Brenner Base Tunnel slips to 2032, with access routes later still The Brenner Base Tunnel is now scheduled to enter service at the end of 2032, and the ScanMed plan warns that further delay remains possible. Several southern access sections will follow after 2030, while the German northern access route is not expected to be completed before 2040. The plan also warns that once Brenner opens, capacity constraints on surrounding sections will already be “real and not hypothetical”, with consequences for international freight. Fehmarnbelt tunnel. Image: © Femern 4. Fehmarnbelt no longer has a reliable opening date The Fehmarnbelt Fixed Link and its German access route are both expected to miss their previous deadlines. Problems with the vessel required to immerse the tunnel elements have delayed the fixed link, while German planning and permitting have slowed the hinterland connection. Denmark and Germany are now drawing up revised commissioning schedules and discussing what the plan calls “a possible new, reliable opening date”. 5. The France–Spain Atlantic missing link slips beyond 2040 The new Dax–Spanish border railway is part of the core network, which is supposed to be completed by 2030, but no completion date has yet been defined and national planning currently points to completion beyond 2040. Preparatory work is still at study stage. The Atlantic coordinator warns that while some corridor sections are expected to be completed after 2030, “further delays, notably on the cross-border section between Spain and France, are not an option”. 6. Emmerich–Oberhausen will remain under reconstruction until at least 2034 On the North Sea–Baltic Corridor, the German upgrade between Emmerich and Oberhausen, one of the main freight connections between the Netherlands and Germany, is not expected to reopen fully until 2034 at the earliest. The project includes a third track and major bridge works and forms part of a wider group of German TEN-T projects which the plan says “face delays and risk missing deadlines”. RFC North Sea – Baltic map. Image: © RFC 7. Several Mediterranean rail projects now run into 2032–34 The Mediterranean plan lists the Lyon–Turin cross-border railway for completion in 2033, and Vicenza–Padova in 2034. The Terzo Valico to the port of Genoa should be ready by 2028, but the rest of the Genoa node will have to wait until 2032/ Vicenza–Padova had previously been targeted for 2029, with the five-year postponement attributed to additional design work and the need to identify the necessary financial resources. rail.title: Погрузка на сети РЖД в октябре может снизиться на 2%
rail.summary_en: Погрузка на сети РЖД по итогам октября 2026 года может составить 94,5 млн тонн, что на 2% ниже уровня прошлого года. Такой прогноз дал аналитик компании «Эйлер» Андрей Полищук.
rail.content: 06.10.2026 10:00:08 Погрузка на сети РЖД по итогам октября 2026 года может составить 94,5 млн тонн, что на 2% ниже уровня прошлого года. Такой прогноз дал аналитик компании «Эйлер» Андрей Полищук. Наиболее заметное снижение ожидается в сегменте нефти и нефтепродуктов — на 12%, до 14,3 млн тонн. Погрузка каменного угля может сократиться на 1%, до 28 млн тонн, зерна — на 5%, до 3,4 млн тонн. Снижение по зерну эксперт связывает с высокой базой прошлого года. При этом грузооборот без учета порожнего пробега может вырасти на 2%, до 217,2 млрд тарифных т-км. rail.content: 06.10.2026 09:37:26 В китайском порту установили рекорд по обработке контейнеров с одного судна Порт Яньтянь в китайском Шэньчжэне установил новый национальный рекорд по объему погрузки и разгрузки контейнеров в рамках одного судозахода. rail.title: «МЦ-Слежение»: все данные о дислокации вагонов по РФ и СНГ в едином окне. Внедрение от 3 дней
rail.summary_en: «МЦ-Слежение» — программный комплекс, разработанный специально для управления парком вагонов. Удобный мониторинг местоположения вагонов, отчеты по дислокации и ремонтам, автоматизация работы с накладными, управление расчетами и еще десятки функций доступны пользователям постоянно.
rail.content: 06.10.2026 09:15:53 « МЦ-Слежение » — программный комплекс, разработанный специально для управления парком вагонов. Удобный мониторинг местоположения вагонов, отчеты по дислокации и ремонтам, автоматизация работы с накладными, управление расчетами и еще десятки функций доступны пользователям постоянно. Какие возможности делают «МЦ-Слежение» одним из лучших в России инструментов для автоматизации в железнодорожной логистике: — Дислокация по РФ и СНГ в едином окне. Система обеспечивает удобную работу с данными о дислокации вагонов и контейнеров на всем пути следования. — Анализ отклонений от плана. Решение позволяет автоматически выявлять брошенные вагоны, перевод в нерабочий парк, простои в пути, на станциях назначения и в ремонте. — Расчет прогноза прибытия. Прогноз времени прибытия обновляется в момент отправления и при фиксации каждой новой операции по ходу движения. Это позволяет оперативно принимать управленческие решения и минимизировать издержки. — Авторассылка отчетов и разметка. Отчеты могут автоматически отправляться на электронную почту сотрудников или контрагентов по заданному расписанию. Например, можно настроить рассылку ежедневного отчета о подходе вагонов. ПК «МЦ-Слежение» надежен: ему уже более 20 лет, и сейчас его используют в ежедневной работе такие компании, как «РН-Транс», «Новая перевозочная компания», «ГТЛК». Вот что говорят о системе : «Программный комплекс „МЦ- Слежение“ является гибким и высокопроизводительным инструментом, позволяющим постоянно развивать функциональность. Сотрудничество с АО „МЦ-Сервис Инжиниринг“ приносит ощутимый эффект в работе и позволяет повышать эффективность бизнес-процессов», — цитата из рекомендации АО «РН-Транс». «Предоставляемый нам в рамках договорных отношений программный комплекс постоянно развивается, — отмечают в ХК „Новотранс“. — Особенно хотелось бы отметить гибкость тонкой настройки под бизнес-процессы нашей организации и возможность интеграции с другими системами». rail.title: Лизинг вагонов: рынок в поисках оптимального решения
rail.content: Рынок лизинга подвижного состава длительное время находится под давлением ряда негативных факторов, и все же адаптируется к ним. На пути к безубыточности О некоторых тенденциях рассказала на конференции «Операторский бизнес: экономика, качество, взаимодействие с рынком» управляющий директор по лизингу подвижного состава, водных и воздушных судов «ВТБ Лизинг» Оксана Ивановская. На сети продолжается кризис доходности оперирования вагонами по основным родам подвижного состава. Сохраняется дисбаланс стоимости владения парком и его прибыльностью. Стоимость услуг операторов по предоставлению в аренду вагонов за последнее время пошла вверх, и хотя разница между лизинговым платежом и ставкой доходности по основным типам подвижного состава остается отрицательной, этот спред сокращается. Сегодня по некоторым типам парка он не превышает 400 руб./сут. за вагон (например, у инновационного вагона – 299 руб.), хотя ранее был существенно выше 1 тыс. руб. С одной стороны, появляются факторы, поддерживающие железнодорожный операторский бизнес, например, снижается конкуренция со стороны автотранспорта из-за топливного кризиса, с другой, возникают новые риски, к примеру, проблема с вывозом грузов через Азово-Черноморский бассейн. Отсюда важно взвешенное решение, как со стороны лизингополучателей, так и финансовых организаций. Сакраментальный вопрос – насколько эффективны инвестиции в вагон в текущих реалиях. Сегодня, к примеру, стоимость инновационного полувагона (срок службы – 32 года) составляет приблизительно 4,8 млн руб. При расчете IRR (внутренняя норма доходности) получается на уровне 12,4%, хотя обычно бизнес ориентируется на 20%, отметила О. Ивановская. В нынешних условиях лизингодатель фокусируется не столько на финансировании нового подвижного состава, сколько на поддержку действующих договоров с клиентами: реструктуризацию, внедрение дополнительных продуктов в виде дополнительных займов на ремонт вагонов, когда это целесообразно (за последний год-полтора капитальный ремонт полувагонов заметно подорожал – теперь он превышает 1 млн руб., как и других родов видов подвижного состава), займов на операционную деятельность, связанную с эксплуатацией парка под обеспечение уже имеющимися в лизинге вагонами. Ставки аренды еще низкие, но все же растут Рынок приближается к точке безубыточности, констатирует представитель «ВТБ-Лизинг», что вселяет определенный оптимизм на дальнейшее развитие событий. Хотя постройка вагонов в стране сокращается второй год подряд (за 8 месяцев этого года произведено парка на 27% ниже, чем в прошлом, и в 1,7 раза меньше результата за аналогичный период позапрошлого), в последнее время происходит определенное помесячное увеличение выпуска, обращает внимание руководитель проектов (аналитика и консалтинг) ROLLINGSTOCK Agency Александр Слободяник. Темпы падения производства относительно 2025 года сокращаются. Если в I квартале этого года отставание было 45-48%, то июльский результат оказался ниже соответствующего за прошлый год уже на 3,5%, а августовский выпуск превзошел объем прошлогоднего за аналогичный месяц более чем на 5%. Если анализировать по родам подвижного состава, то драйвером остаются цистерны, уточнил А. Слободяник. В прошлом году их было выпущено рекордное количество, и в текущем они еще тоже сохраняют положительную динамику. В целом же цены на подвижной состав с начала 2025 года постепенно сокращались. Одновременно снижалась ставка ЦБ, пусть и не столь существенными темпами. После достижения минимального уровня ставки аренды вагонов в начале 2026 года начали увеличиваться. Конечно, им далеко до пиковых периодов 2023-2024 годов, но все же рост произошел, отмечает эксперт. Правда, расчеты показывают, что несмотря на эти факторы, подвижной состав для бизнеса пока не окупается. В настоящее время львиная доля новых вагонов приобретается собственниками, прежде всего это различные кэптивные компании, в целях обеспечения транспортной безопасности, резюмирует А. Слободяник. rail.title: РЖД запустят новые двухэтажные поезда в Адлер из Самары и Казани
rail.summary_en: РЖД планируют в конце октября вывести на маршруты новые двухэтажные поезда, которые свяжут Самару и Казань с Адлером и будут следовать через Ростов-на-Дону.
rail.content: 05.10.2026 18:00:31 РЖД запустят новые двухэтажные поезда в Адлер из Самары и Казани РЖД планируют в конце октября вывести на маршруты новые двухэтажные поезда, которые свяжут Самару и Казань с Адлером и будут следовать через Ростов-на-Дону. Поезд № 337/338 будет курсировать между Самарой и Адлером, а состав № 385/386 – между Казанью и Адлером. К новогодним праздникам перевозчик также планирует запустить дополнительный поезд по маршруту Киров – Адлер. Он также будет следовать через Ростовскую область. Билеты на рейсы, отправляющиеся с 30 декабря, уже поступили в продажу. Кроме того, в период зимних каникул пассажирам будут доступны туристические поезда. В их числе – «Лыжная стрела», которая будет курсировать до горного курорта Роза Хутор. Одновременно с 1 октября изменилась стоимость проезда в регулируемом сегменте поездов дальнего следования. По данным Ассоциации туроператоров России, повышение затронуло билеты в плацкартные и общие вагоны, а также перевозку багажа. Стоимость поездок в купейных вагонах и СВ в рамках этого повышения не изменилась. rail.title: В Казахстане за пять лет построили более 900 км новых железных дорог
rail.summary_en: За последние пять лет в Казахстане проложили 911 км новых железнодорожных путей. Сейчас в стране продолжается строительство еще около 800 км железных дорог, сообщили в пресс-службе правительства республики.
rail.content: 05.10.2026 17:43:10 За последние пять лет в Казахстане проложили 911 км новых железнодорожных путей. Сейчас в стране продолжается строительство еще около 800 км железных дорог, сообщили в пресс-службе правительства республики. Одновременно ведется модернизация существующей железнодорожной инфраструктуры. Работы охватывают порядка 2,6 тыс. км действующих путей. Продолжается развитие и пассажирских перевозок. В 2023–2025 годах железнодорожным транспортом в Казахстане воспользовались в общей сложности 60,2 млн пассажиров. С начала 2026 года поезда АО «Пассажирские перевозки» перевезли 7,5 млн человек. Наибольший пассажиропоток приходится на Алматы, Астану и Шымкент, а также область Абай, Актюбинскую, Карагандинскую, Кызылординскую и Жамбылскую области. Параллельно на железнодорожном транспорте расширяются социальные и специализированные сервисы. В частности, женские вагоны сейчас курсируют по 13 направлениям. С момента запуска этой услугой воспользовались 946 тыс. пассажирок. Для пассажиров с инвалидностью и сопровождающих их лиц предусмотрена скидка в размере 50% на проезд по социально значимым маршрутам. За семь месяцев 2026 года для них было оформлено 396 тыс. билетов на специализированные места.
